title: Prince George Home Energy Rebates 2026: Up to $16,000 With the Northern Top-Up
desc: Prince George rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, including the northern top-up that raises CleanBC Level 1 to $16,000.
badge: CleanBC up to $16,000 with the northern top-up
lead: Prince George qualifies for CleanBC's northern top-up, the only way to reach $16,000. It also has the oldest housing in the interior (62% built before 1981) and a record low of -42.4°C.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Prince George in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Northern top-up
cards.note: Added to CleanBC Level 1 and 2 amounts for homes at or north of 100 Mile House on BC Hydro service.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: Homes at or north of 100 Mile House on BC Hydro service get an extra $3,000 for a central, multi-split or two mini-split heat pump, or $1,500 for a single head, on CleanBC Level 1 and 2 only. Level 1 at $13,000 plus $3,000 makes $16,000 for a fossil-fuel home. Prince George and Fort St. John qualify.

The 2021 Census counted 31,795 households. 62% live in homes built before 1981, the second-highest share in the group, and 58% live in detached houses, the highest. 68% own. 10,470 are owner-occupied detached houses from before 1981. Major repairs were reported by 6.5%.

The January average low is -9.7°C and the record in 2015 to 2024 was -42.4°C. A heat pump in this climate needs to be a cold-climate model and the installer should state its output at -25°C or below. Insulation first, then equipment.

For electric-heated houses BC Hydro pays up to $4,000 for a heat pump, up to $5,500 for insulation, up to $2,000 for windows and up to $1,000 for a water heater. Solar gets about 3.21 peak sun hours a day.
